defects: Longest shot is 5.9 s. The closing pull-back to the filmstrip of all the posters is held far too long, and change per second falls to 17, 20 and then 1.1 over the last three seconds.
The pair frames are nearly identical (PAULA TEMPLE, RROSE). Some shots are held posters with only a texture or arc flickering, with no transform in the type or the layout.
The capacitor-disc stack on PAULA TEMPLE is flat, low-detail CG with plain shading. It blocks the artist name and makes the main type unreadable.
The KIA / IDA ENGBERG frame shows two half-panels, with IDA ENGBERG cropped off the bottom. This reads as a transition caught mid-move, not a composed frame.
The cable shot (HÉCTOR OAKS) puts its small orange squares and spark in a weak corner, and the large dead area above the name has no tension.
Glow bloom is uniform across every title. It is a filter look with no light source, and the same halo appears on every word.
The first ~1.8 s of audio is almost silent (low drone only) while the picture is already cutting. The opening has no sonic hook.
gaps: Motion: most shots are static posters swapped on the beat. Top studio work would carry continuous transforms across cuts: the rail, the arc and the current should travel from shot to shot and drive each reveal. Elements need easing, overshoot and weight, and the final pull-back needs to be compressed to under 2 s with a hard button.

Sound: the track is a sparse kick-and-click grid plus one white-noise riser, with a near-empty 11–13 s gap. There are few tonal partials, no bespoke electrical sound design (hum, arcing, relay clunks) tied to each artist's object, and no mix depth. It reads as generated, not produced.

Finish and design: the per-artist metaphors (capacitor, cable, plasma, danger sign, bulbs) don't share one material language or one lighting model. Type is often obscured or cropped, and the type itself does no work: weight, width and timing are never mapped to the current or voltage idea.
